summary: Master risk pooling and insurance in social protection with our specialized training course. Gain valuable insights and skills to advance your career.
lede: Risk pooling and insurance in social protection helps practitioners design schemes that protect people against life-cycle risks, shared shocks, and crises rather than relying only on payments after harm occurs. This course provides a practical way to define risks, compare pooling and insurance options, and make informed choices about who contributes and who benefits. You will assess equity and financial sustainability while exploring social health insurance, unemployment insurance, crop and livestock insurance, and disaster risk financing. Through applied cases and design exercises, you will examine contribution and benefit structures and weigh the trade-offs between coverage, cost, and fairness.
audienceIntro: This course is strategically designed for professionals who regularly make or influence decisions on social protection design, insurance mechanisms, and risk management.
audience: Social protection program managers and policy makers
Officials in ministries of finance, labor, health
Social insurance agency managers and technical staff
Staff in NGOs and international organizations
Disaster risk management and climate resilience specialists
Actuarial, finance, or risk officers embedded
modules: Foundations of Social Protection and Risk Pooling
Principles of Insurance for Social Protection Practitioners
Financing and Sustainability of Social Insurance Schemes
Integrating Insurance with Social Assistance and Safety Nets
Climate and Disaster Risk Financing in Social Protection
Governance, Regulation, and Accountability in Social Insurance
Communicating Design Choices and Building Stakeholder Buy-in
prerequisites: Participants should have a basic understanding of social protection systems and a willingness to engage with financial and risk concepts. Experience in social program design or management is highly beneficial.
